title: Feature branches
summary: Exercise 2: branch off develop, name it right, commit twice.

steps.title: Why branches
steps.say: A branch is your own line of work. `main` stays production-ready, `develop` collects finished features, and each feature gets its own branch.

board.code:
main      o----------------------o   (only finished, tested work)
develop   o-------o--------o-----o   (features merge in here)
issue-12       \--o--o--/          (your work, off develop)

steps.title: Make one
steps.say: Start from `develop`, then create and switch to your branch in one command.

board.code:
git checkout develop
git checkout -b issue-12-turbo-boost

marks.label: create the branch, then switch to it

steps.title: Open a terminal
steps.say: These exercises are easiest in the terminal.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.say: `cd 02-feature-branch`, then run the two commands above.

steps.title: Which branch am I on?
steps.say: The bottom-left corner shows the branch the editor is looking at. It's the quickest check before you commit.

steps.title: Two commits
steps.say: The exercise wants **two separate** commits: small commits, each with a clear message, tell the story of the work.

board.code:
git add FEATURES.md
git commit -m "Describe the turbo boost button"
# edit again...
git add FEATURES.md
git commit -m "Add the turbo boost speed limit"

steps.title: Check it
steps.say: Run `git log --oneline` to see your two commits on top of the starting one.
